questions.q: What's the relationship between the built-in Contributor role and Data Factory Contributor?
options: Contributor is a superset — it includes everything Data Factory Contributor grants, plus more
They grant exactly identical, non-overlapping permissions
Data Factory Contributor is a superset of Contributor
They have nothing to do with each other
questions.explain: Contributor is a superset role — if someone already has Contributor at the resource group level, granting Data Factory Contributor too adds nothing extra.

questions.q: Does deploying a Resource Manager template with the Data Factory Contributor role elevate your permissions?
options: No — if the template tries to create a resource type you don't have permission for, the deployment fails
Yes — it grants you permission to create any Azure resource type
Only for virtual machines specifically
Only when deploying from the Azure portal, not PowerShell
questions.explain: Data Factory Contributor doesn't quietly elevate permissions — a template deployment that requires creating a resource type you can't otherwise create will fail with an authorization error.

questions.q: Why does the scope where you assign a role matter?
options: The same role grants access to everything at or below that scope — resource group level reaches every factory in it, individual factory level reaches only that one
Scope has no real effect on what a role actually grants
Roles can only ever be assigned at the subscription level
Scope only matters for the Reader role, not Contributor
questions.explain: Data Factory Contributor at the resource group level can manage any factory in that group, while Contributor scoped to one specific factory can only touch that single resource.

questions.q: What does the "can edit, can't publish" pattern rely on?
options: Git repo permissions and Data Factory permissions being independent of each other
A special "draft-only" role that doesn't actually exist
Disabling the Publish button for all users of a data factory
Requiring two-factor authentication specifically for publishing
questions.explain: Because repo write access and Data Factory role are separate, a Data Factory Reader with repo write access can edit and commit changes, but can't publish them to the live factory.

questions.q: Which built-in role fits a user who should only view and monitor a data factory, with no edits?
options: Reader
Owner
Data Factory Contributor
There's no role that supports view-only access
questions.explain: The built-in Reader role, assigned on the data factory resource, lets a user view and monitor without granting any edit or publish capability.
